name: driver-static
description: sky130 FS line driver (design/differential_driver.sch): static VOH/VOL, total output resistance, enable truth table and disabled-pad leakage across the 45-point PVT matrix.
claim: Static behaviour of the sky130 FS line driver over the 45-point PVT matrix against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 rows 'Output voltage swing, static' (VOH 2.8-3.6 V, VOL 0.0-0.3 V; loads per USB 2.0 section 7.1.1.1, plus the literal 1.5 kohm-to-3.6 V reading for VOH) and 'Driver output resistance' (28-44 ohm), plus the drive-enable/OE truth table; disabled-pad leakage as engineering data (no ratified limit exists and none is applied). Schematic-level, deterministic, no mismatch (no Monte Carlo), no passive-process spread, no layout parasitics; not a signoff claim.

leak_dp_max_na.spice: .meas dc leak_dp_max_na MAX i(vsap) FROM=0 TO=3.6

leak_dp_min_na.spice: .meas dc leak_dp_min_na MIN i(vsap) FROM=0 TO=3.6

leak_dm_max_na.spice: .meas dc leak_dm_max_na MAX i(vsbm) FROM=0 TO=3.6

leak_dm_min_na.spice: .meas dc leak_dm_min_na MIN i(vsbm) FROM=0 TO=3.6

record.netlist_provenance: schematic-derived netlist: xschem export of design/differential_driver.sch (design/netlist/differential_driver.spice, byte-identical to the deck frozen in the snapshot below) plus the testbench deck; no layout, no parasitic extraction
record.statistical_convention: deterministic PVT corners only (5 process x 3 temperature x 3 supply). Mismatch / Monte Carlo was NOT run. The five sky130 process sections tt/ff/ss/fs/sf all load the typical resistor and capacitor parameters (r+c/res_typical__cap_typical), so poly-resistor sheet and MIM-capacitor process spread are NOT covered by this record; resistor temperature coefficients are (+ resistor and MOS temperature behaviour at -40/27/100 C).
record.bounds: the ratified limits and engineering criteria in the Method section (tb.json checks)
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level electrical evidence for one block against ratified spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 rows. It does not claim layout, DRC/LVS, mismatch, passive-process spread, level shifting or signoff, and does not relax any target. A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.
method: Supply = swept I/O rail vsup (3.0 / 3.3 / 3.6 V). Inputs are VDD-domain logic: logic 1 wired to the supply node, logic 0 to ground. One DC sweep of the forcing source vf (0-3.65 V, 50 mV step; the sweep runs one step past 3.6 V so that the 3.6 V point is interior; max/min are taken over 0-3.6 V only) is the only analysis; every quantity other than the leakage sweep is sweep-independent and read at the first point (AT=0). Each test uses its own copy of the driver.

VOH/VOL load conditions, from the USB 2.0 specification section 7.1.1.1 (full-speed driver characteristics): the static output must be below VOL(max) 0.3 V with a 1.5 kohm load to 3.6 V and above VOH(min) 2.8 V with a 15 kohm load to ground. `voh_*_v`: driven high (TXDx=1, DRVEN=OE=1) into 15 kohm to ground; `vol_*_v`: driven low into 1.5 kohm to 3.6 V. The ratified row's parenthetical '(1.5 kohm pull-up to 3.6 V)' sits on the VOH/VOL cell as a whole; the literal reading for VOH is measured too (`voh15_*_v`: driven high into 1.5 kohm to 3.6 V) and checked against the same 2.8-3.6 V. The reading of the parenthetical is raised in spec/decision-records/0004-fs-driver-voh-vol-load-conditions.md (proposed); no ratified value is changed.

Driver output resistance (total, enabled, static): the pad is forced by an ideal source 0.3 V away from the rail the driver is pulling to (VDD - 0.3 V when driving high, 0.3 V when driving low); R = 0.3 V / |I(pad)|. This is a large-signal resistance at the static drive point, includes the output FET on-resistance (P for high, N for low) and the series poly resistor RSER, and is checked for each line and each polarity against 28-44 ohm.

Enable truth table: all four TXDP/TXDM data combinations (including SE0 = 00 and 11) x all four DRVEN/OE combinations, each pad loaded by 10 kohm to VDD/2, so a driven 1, a driven 0 and a released pad are distinct. Functional bounds (fractions of the corner supply, engineering criteria, not USB limits): driven 1 >= 0.95, driven 0 <= 0.05, released (DRVEN=0 or OE=0) within 0.48-0.52. Names `tt_<line>_d<TXDP><TXDM>_e<DRVEN><OE>_v`.

Disabled-pad leakage (engineering data, no ratified limit, none applied): instance lka disabled by OE=0 (DRVEN=1, TXDP=1), D+ forced by vf from 0 to 3.6 V while D- is held at VDD/2; instance lkb disabled by DRVEN=0 (OE=1, TXDM=1), D- forced by vf while D+ is held at VDD/2. Current positive out of the pad into the forcing source; reported at 0 / 1.5 / 3.0 / 3.6 V and its max/min over the sweep; `leak_*_mid_na` is the held line's current. Forcing above the corner supply (up to 3.6 V at a 3.0 V rail) forward-biases the output PMOS drain junction; that current is part of the data.
`isup_static_ua`: supply current of one extra driver instance enabled and driving J (TXDP=1, TXDM=0) into open pads: bias plus leakage; data only.
A missing or non-finite value of any measurement fails the corner (harness rule).

resistor-sets.claim: Static behaviour of the sky130 FS line driver over the 225-point resistor-set matrix (5 MOS corners x 5 global resistor/capacitor parameter sets x 3 temperature x 3 supply; sim/corners-resistor-sets.json, spec/decision-records/0005-resistor-sheet-resistance-corner-coverage.md) against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 rows 'Output voltage swing, static' (VOH 2.8-3.6 V, VOL 0.0-0.3 V; loads per USB 2.0 section 7.1.1.1, plus the literal 1.5 kohm-to-3.6 V reading for VOH) and 'Driver output resistance' (28-44 ohm inclusive, unchanged), plus the drive-enable/OE truth table; disabled-pad leakage as engineering data (no ratified limit exists and none is applied). Schematic-level, deterministic, no mismatch (no Monte Carlo), no per-device spread, no layout parasitics; not a signoff claim.

record.statistical_convention: deterministic corners only (5 MOS corners x 5 global resistor/capacitor parameter sets x 3 temperature x 3 supply = 225 points); mismatch / Monte Carlo was NOT run. The suffixed sections (ll, hh, hl, lh) select the pinned library's res_low/res_high and cap_low/cap_high sets together with the matching drawn-width tolerances (tol_*); the driver's series poly resistor (res_generic_po), bias resistor (res_xhigh_po_1p41) and MIM edge-rate capacitors respond through those parameters, so these are the PDK's own global sheet-resistance and capacitor corners but they are not resistor-only sections, and the PDK ships them as global corners (all resistors and capacitors move together), not as per-device spread

Resistor/capacitor coverage: each point's process section is one of 25 pinned-library sections = 5 MOS corners x {typical, ll, hh, hl, lh}; the section -> (MOS file, resistor set, capacitor set) mapping and the resolved library includes are recorded in evidence.json (`sections`) and checked by the lint against the approved map (sim/corners-resistor-sets.json, spec/decision-records/0005-resistor-sheet-resistance-corner-coverage.md). The bare sections `ll`, `hh`, `hl`, `lh` carry the tt MOS corner.

Compatibility: every bound and check above is unchanged and applies at all 225 points; this record is a supplement to, not a replacement for, the 45-point records (res_typical only), which are unchanged and keep their own frozen matrix.
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level electrical evidence for one block against ratified spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 rows over the PDK's global resistor/capacitor corner sets (series poly resistor, bias resistor, MIM capacitors). It does not claim layout, DRC/LVS, mismatch, per-device passive spread, Monte Carlo, level shifting or signoff, and does not relax any target (the 28-44 ohm output-resistance row is applied unchanged at every point). A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.
